issue_title: bug(gui): performance tab's entrance-pupil and object-distance controls do not affect calculations
issue_body:
## Summary

The performance tab reads an "Entrance Pupil" and an "Object Distance" from its spin boxes, prints them in the report as calculation parameters, and never passes either to the aberration calculation. Changing them changes only the two text lines, not the aberrations, f-number, spot size, or any other metric.

## Impact

- Misleading UI: the report presents values as inputs when they are labels.
- A user can believe a design was evaluated at a 1000 mm object distance or a 10 mm pupil when nothing changed.
- `AberrationsCalculator` does expose `object_distance_mm`, but the GUI never supplies it (and the implementation rejects finite object distances), so the control cannot work as shown.

## Evidence

- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:151-156` — Entrance Pupil spin box.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:172-177` — Object Distance spin box.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:351-354` — both values read from the widgets.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:404-406` — `calculate_all_aberrations()` called with only `field_angle_deg` and `wavelength_nm`.
- `openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py:455-461` — values printed as "Calculation Parameters".

Repro with Entrance Pupil 10 mm / Object Distance 1000 mm, then 100 mm / 100 mm:

```text
first  parameter lines: ['Entrance Pupil: 10.00 mm', 'Object Distance: 1000.0 mm']
second parameter lines: ['Entrance Pupil: 100.00 mm', 'Object Distance: 100.0 mm']
report identical apart from those two lines: True
first f/# line: ['f-number (f/#): 2.43']
second f/# line: ['f-number (f/#): 2.43']
```

## Expected behaviour

Either the controls feed the calculation (pupil size for aperture-dependent metrics, object distance for finite-conjugate aberrations) or they are removed/disabled and the report stops presenting them as inputs.

## Suggested fix

Pass the object distance into `calculate_all_aberrations(object_distance_mm=...)` once the calculator supports finite conjugates; derive the f-number and pupil-dependent metrics from the entrance-pupil value. If finite-conjugate support is out of scope, remove the two spin boxes and the report lines until it lands. Add a GUI test asserting the metric changes when the pupil/object-distance value changes.
pr_title: fix(gui): make the performance tab evaluate its entrance pupil
pr_body:
## Description

The Performance tab read an "Entrance Pupil" spin box, printed the value in its
report as a calculation parameter, and built the aberration calculator without
it. Every pupil produced the same numbers:

```
Entrance Pupil: 10.00 mm      Entrance Pupil: 100.00 mm
f-number (f/#): 3.89          f-number (f/#): 3.89
```

The "Object Distance" spin box was worse. `AberrationsCalculator` raises for a
finite `object_distance_mm` - every Seidel estimator assumes an object at
infinity - so the widget's 1000 mm was never usable, yet the report presented
it as the distance the design had been evaluated at.

## What changed

- **`openlens/aberrations.py`** - `AberrationsCalculator` takes an optional
  `entrance_pupil_mm`. It is validated (positive, finite), clamped to the
  element's physical clear aperture (the glass cannot pass more light) and
  used for every aperture-derived quantity: f-number, numerical aperture,
  Airy disk, the marginal-ray traces, and the field metrics. The result
  dictionaries report the effective value as `"entrance_pupil"`.
- **`openlens/gui/tabs/performance_tab.py`** - the tab passes its widget value
  to the calculator and prints the effective (clamped) pupil, so the report
  can no longer show one aperture and evaluate another.
- The finite object-distance control is removed. The report states the actual
  model condition: `Object Distance: infinity (collimated; finite conjugates
  are not modelled)`.

The visible consequence: a 25 mm f/3.9 singlet evaluated at a 10 mm pupil now
reports f/9.7, with the correspondingly larger Airy disk, and moving the
control changes those numbers.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Related Issues

Closes #620

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Added regression tests that fail before this change and pass after
- [x] `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen OPENLENS_SKIP_SLOW=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`
- [x] `black --line-length=100 openlens/ tests/ --check`
- [x] `ruff check`, `flake8`, `mypy`

New module `tests/test_aberrations_entrance_pupil.py` - eleven tests fail on
the unfixed code (`TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'entrance_pupil_mm'`):

- `test_the_default_is_the_physical_clear_aperture`
- `test_the_result_reports_the_effective_pupil`
- `test_the_f_number_follows_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_the_numerical_aperture_follows_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_the_airy_disk_follows_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_the_spherical_aberration_shrinks_with_the_pupil`
- `test_a_pupil_wider_than_the_lens_is_clamped`
- `test_a_system_target_honours_the_entrance_pupil`
- `test_a_pupil_as_large_as_the_lens_changes_nothing`
- `test_a_non_positive_pupil_raises` / `test_a_non_finite_pupil_raises` /
  `test_a_non_numeric_pupil_raises`

New module `tests/test_performance_tab_entrance_pupil.py` drives the real tab
with an inline worker; four of its five tests fail on the unfixed code:

- `test_the_report_evaluates_the_pupil_it_shows`
- `test_changing_the_pupil_changes_the_f_number`
- `test_a_pupil_wider_than_the_lens_is_reported_clamped`
- `test_the_object_distance_is_stated_as_infinity`
- `test_the_finite_object_distance_control_is_gone`

Full local suite: `Ran 2733 tests ... OK (skipped=35)`; the aberration,
performance-tab, image-simulation and end-to-end suites (151 tests) pass.
